Fact.Name: Social Security (OASDI) wage base TY2026
Fact.Description: TY2026 OASDI contribution and benefit base = $184,500. #166: SSA, "Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026", 90 FR 49047 (Nov. 3, 2025), https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-19763 (PDF https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-11-03/pdf/2025-19763.pdf), p. 49050: "The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026."

Fact.Name: SE tax filing threshold
Fact.Description: Net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more generally require Schedule SE / SE tax. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE optional-method maximum income
Fact.Description: TY2026 Schedule SE Part II line 14, "Maximum income for optional methods," $7,560. 26 U.S.C. 1402(l)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#l_1): the lower limit is the sum of the Social Security Act section 213(d) quarter-of-coverage amounts for each calendar quarter ending with or within the taxable year. SSA, "Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026," 90 FR 49047 (Nov. 3, 2025), p. 49051: "The earnings required for a quarter of coverage in 2026 is $1,890." Four quarters times $1,890 is $7,560. 26 U.S.C. 1402(l)(2) sets the upper limit at 150 percent of that lower limit ($11,340), the farm gross-income threshold, not line 14. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), PDF p. 3, line 14. Line 15 (the farm optional method) stays blank because farm self-employment stops the return, so line 16 equals this amount.

Fact.Name: Nonfarm optional method net-profit limit
Fact.Description: Net nonfarm profits must be less than $8,186. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, Part II: "your net nonfarm profits were less than $8,186 and also less than 72.189% of your gross nonfarm income." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 7, same test. Net nonfarm profits here are Schedule C line 31. A nonzero Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A together with the election stops the return instead of being included.

Fact.Name: Nonfarm optional method gross-income percentage
Fact.Description: 72.189% of gross nonfarm income. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, and 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7: net nonfarm profits must be "less than 72.189% of your gross nonfarm income." Gross nonfarm income here is Schedule C line 7. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code C is not collected.

Fact.Name: Nonfarm optional method two-thirds of gross nonfarm income
Fact.Description: Part II line 17 is two-thirds of gross nonfarm income, not below zero, and not more than line 16. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, line 17: "Enter the smaller of: two-thirds (2/3) of gross nonfarm income ... (not less than zero) or the amount on line 16."

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 3
Fact.Description: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss) plus nonfarm Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A. The sum can be a loss. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), PDF p. 2, line 2: "Net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31; and Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A (other than farming)"; line 3: "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 2". Line 1a is farm profit, including farm partnerships' box 14 code A. Farm profit, the farm optional method, church employee income, ministry or a Form 4361 or 4029 exemption, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages stop the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope) instead of being entered as zero. The nonfarm optional method skips line 2 when /primaryFilerNonfarmOptionalMethodApplies is true. An election that is not allowed stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethod). Box 14 code A is scheduleE /scheduleEK1Box14CodeANonfarmTotal. A reduction, farming, a limited-partner amount that is not only guaranteed payments (26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(13)), a joint return, or an S corporation amount stops the return (scheduleE /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIIBox14CodeA and the matching stops; 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 5, Partnership Income or Loss) instead of filing line 2 without the amount or on the wrong spouse's Schedule SE. Schedule C qualified business income together with a nonzero box 14 code A stops the return (form8995 /flowKnockoutScheduleCQbiAndK1Box14CodeA) because the deductible part of self-employment tax is not split between the trades (Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi)). An unanswered K-1 question also stops the print (scheduleE /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartII). With lines 1a and 1b blank, line 3 equals line 2, so the same amount is printed on both. Line 4a is $0 when this amount is not more than zero. Each spouse files their own Schedule SE: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE. Include the total profits or losses from all businesses on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Enter the combined SE tax on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4."

Fact.Name: Primary filer: net earnings from self-employment (Schedule SE line 4a)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4a: "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35% (0.9235)". Otherwise line 4a is $0, including when line 2 is a loss. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(12) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a_12): the deduction equals net earnings times one-half of the sum of the 1401(a) and (b) rates, so 1 - (12.4% + 2.9%) / 2 = 0.9235.

Fact.Name: Primary filer has Schedule C nonfarm activity
Fact.Description: True when this filer's Schedule C line 31 is not zero or Schedule C line 7 is not zero. A filer with neither is not tested for the nonfarm optional method. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, Part II footnotes: net nonfarm profits from Schedule C line 31, and gross nonfarm income from Schedule C line 7.

Fact.Name: Primary filer meets the nonfarm optional method dollar tests
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31 is less than $8,186 (/seNonfarmOptionalMethodNetProfitLimit) and less than 72.189% of Schedule C line 7 (/seNonfarmOptionalMethodGrossIncomeRatio). 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, and 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: two-thirds of gross nonfarm income, limited by line 16
Fact.Description: Smaller of two-thirds of Schedule C line 7, not below zero, and Part II line 16. Line 15 is zero because the farm optional method stops the return, so line 16 is /seOptionalMethodMaximumIncome ($7,560). 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, lines 16 and 17. Rounded to whole dollars the same way line 4a is rounded.

Fact.Name: Primary filer may use the nonfarm optional method on the dollar tests
Fact.Description: The dollar tests are met, and the line 17 amount is at least actual net earnings from the regular method (/primaryFilerSeNetEarnings). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7: "you can't report less than your actual net earnings from nonfarm self-employment."

Fact.Name: Primary filer uses the nonfarm optional method
Fact.Description: True when the filer elects the nonfarm optional method, Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A is not nonzero, this filer has Schedule C activity, the dollar tests are met, line 17 is at least actual net earnings, net earnings from self-employment were at least $400 in 2 of the prior 3 years, and the method has been used fewer than five prior years. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) (the nonfarm optional-method sentences) and 1402(l). False when the election is unanswered or no, so the regular method still computes. An election that is not allowed stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethod).

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE lines 2 and 3
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 2: "Skip line 2 if you use the nonfarm optional method." With lines 1a and 1b blank, line 3 equals line 2. When /primaryFilerNonfarmOptionalMethodApplies is true, both are $0. Otherwise this is /primaryFilerSeNetProfit.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 4a as reported
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4a: if line 3 is more than zero, multiply by 92.35%; otherwise enter line 3. Skipping line 2 makes line 3 and line 4a $0 when the nonfarm optional method applies. Otherwise this is the regular-method amount /primaryFilerSeNetEarnings.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 4b
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4b: "If you elect one or both of the optional methods, enter the total of lines 15 and 17 here." Line 15 is $0, so line 4b equals line 17 when the nonfarm optional method applies, and $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE Part II line 16
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, line 16: "Subtract line 15 from line 14." Line 15 is $0 and line 14 is /seOptionalMethodMaximumIncome ($7,560) when the nonfarm optional method applies. Otherwise $0, printed blank.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE Part II line 17
Fact.Description: Line 17 when the nonfarm optional method applies; otherwise $0. The same amount is line 4b. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, line 17: "Also, include this amount on line 4b above."

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 4c
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4c: "Combine lines 4a and 4b." When the nonfarm optional method applies, line 4a is $0 and line 4c equals line 4b. Otherwise line 4b is $0 and line 4c equals the regular-method line 4a. Later lines use this amount.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: SE tax applies
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4c: "If less than $400, stop; you don’t owe self-employment tax." 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_2): no self-employment income when net earnings are "less than $400". The test is line 4c, per individual, so an optional-method line 4b of $400 or more is self-employment income even when line 4a is zero.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: total W-2 box 3 social security wages
Fact.Description: Sum of the primary filer's W-2 box 3 amounts, part of Schedule SE line 8a ("Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2)"). 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1) reduces the base by "the amount of the wages paid to such individual", so only this filer's own W-2s count.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: total W-2 box 7 social security tips
Fact.Description: Sum of the primary filer's W-2 box 7 amounts, the rest of Schedule SE line 8a. 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Line 8b (Form 4137) and line 8c (Form 8919). Form 4137 tips stop the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips). A yes on /hadForm8919Wages stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). An answered no leaves line 8c blank, and income /wagesFrom8919 is $0.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 9
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 7 "$184,500" (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026) minus line 8d, not below zero: line 9 "Subtract line 8d from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0- here and on line 10". 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1): self-employment income excludes the part above "(i) an amount equal to the contribution and benefit base ... minus (ii) the amount of the wages paid to such individual during such taxable years".

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8a: Total social security wages and tips
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, created 4/27/26), form page 1, line 8a: "Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2) and railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation." W-2 box 3 (/primaryFilerOasdiWagesTotal) plus box 7 (/primaryFilerOasdiTipsTotal) for the person with self-employment income; railroad retirement compensation is not collected. Wage-base coordination under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Printed only; the tax itself uses /primaryFilerSeRemainingSocialSecurityWageBase.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8d
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf), form page 1, line 8d: "Add lines 8a, 8b, and 8c." Line 8b (Form 4137 unreported tips) stops the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips). A yes on /hadForm8919Wages stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope), and an answered no leaves line 8c blank (income /wagesFrom8919 is $0), so line 8d = line 8a. Line 8a says "If $184,500 or more, skip lines 8b through 10, and go to line 11", so line 8d is $0 (printed blank) when line 8a is at least the TY2026 wage base (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026, $184,500; 90 FR 49047, p. 49050; 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)).

Fact.Name: Primary filer: smaller of Schedule SE line 6 or line 9
Fact.Description: Base for Schedule SE line 10 ("Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)"); $0 when SE tax doesn't apply (line 4c).

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 10
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 10: "Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)". 26 U.S.C. 1401(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401#a): "a tax equal to 12.4 percent of the amount of the self-employment income for such taxable year".

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 6
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 6 (line 4c plus line 5b; church employee income stops the return when /hadChurchEmployeeIncome is yes), and $0 when line 4c is under $400 ("stop; you don’t owe self-employment tax"). Line 4c already includes line 4b. Feeds line 11 and Form 8959 line 13.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 11
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 11: "Multiply line 6 by 2.9% (0.029)". 26 U.S.C. 1401(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401#b_1): "2.9 percent of the amount of the self-employment income". No wage base applies.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 12
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 12: "Self-employment tax. Add lines 10 and 11."

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 13
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 13: "Deduction for one-half of self-employment tax. Multiply line 12 by 50% (0.50)", rounded to whole dollars as printed on that filer's Schedule SE. 26 U.S.C. 164(f)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164#f): "an amount equal to one-half of the taxes imposed by section 1401 (other than the taxes imposed by section 1401(b)(2))".

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 3
Fact.Description: Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss) from all of their businesses (2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 3: "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 2"), floored at $0 for the regular method. The nonfarm optional method, when /secondaryFilerNonfarmOptionalMethodApplies is true, skips this amount and uses Part II line 17. The farm optional method stops the return. Each spouse files their own Schedule SE: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE. Include the total profits or losses from all businesses on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Enter the combined SE tax on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4."

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: net earnings from self-employment (Schedule SE line 4a)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4a: "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35% (0.9235)". 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(12) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a_12): the deduction equals net earnings times one-half of the sum of the 1401(a) and (b) rates, so 1 - (12.4% + 2.9%) / 2 = 0.9235.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer has Schedule C nonfarm activity
Fact.Description: True when this filer's Schedule C line 31 is not zero or Schedule C line 7 is not zero. On a return that is not a joint return both amounts are $0, so the optional method is not applied to the secondary filer. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, Part II footnotes.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer meets the nonfarm optional method dollar tests
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31 is less than $8,186 and less than 72.189% of Schedule C line 7. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, and 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7. The comparison uses the unfloored Schedule C result, not the regular-method floor at zero.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: two-thirds of gross nonfarm income, limited by line 16
Fact.Description: Smaller of two-thirds of this filer's Schedule C line 7, not below zero, and $7,560. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, lines 16 and 17. Line 15 is zero because the farm optional method stops the return.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer may use the nonfarm optional method on the dollar tests
Fact.Description: The dollar tests are met, and the line 17 amount is at least actual net earnings from the regular method (/secondaryFilerSeNetEarnings). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7: "you can't report less than your actual net earnings from nonfarm self-employment."

Fact.Name: Secondary filer uses the nonfarm optional method
Fact.Description: Same election and prior-year tests as the primary filer, applied to this filer's Schedule C. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) and 1402(l). False when the election is unanswered or no.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 4a as reported
Fact.Description: $0 when the nonfarm optional method applies, because line 2 is skipped. Otherwise the regular-method amount /secondaryFilerSeNetEarnings. 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4a.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 4b
Fact.Description: Line 17 when the nonfarm optional method applies, because line 15 is $0. Otherwise $0. 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4b.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 4c
Fact.Description: Line 4a plus line 4b. 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 4c. Later lines of this filer's Schedule SE use this amount.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: SE tax applies
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4c: "If less than $400, stop; you don’t owe self-employment tax." 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_2): no self-employment income when net earnings are "less than $400". The test is line 4c, per individual.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: total W-2 box 3 social security wages
Fact.Description: Sum of the secondary filer's W-2 box 3 amounts, part of Schedule SE line 8a ("Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2)"). 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1) reduces the base by "the amount of the wages paid to such individual", so only this filer's own W-2s count.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: total W-2 box 7 social security tips
Fact.Description: Sum of the secondary filer's W-2 box 7 amounts, the rest of Schedule SE line 8a. 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Line 8b (Form 4137) and line 8c (Form 8919). Form 4137 tips stop the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips). A yes on /hadForm8919Wages stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). An answered no leaves line 8c blank, and income /wagesFrom8919 is $0.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 9
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 7 "$184,500" (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026) minus line 8d, not below zero: line 9 "Subtract line 8d from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0- here and on line 10". 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1): self-employment income excludes the part above "(i) an amount equal to the contribution and benefit base ... minus (ii) the amount of the wages paid to such individual during such taxable years".

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: smaller of Schedule SE line 6 or line 9
Fact.Description: Base for Schedule SE line 10 ("Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)"); $0 when SE tax doesn't apply (line 4c).

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 10
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 10: "Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)". 26 U.S.C. 1401(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401#a): "a tax equal to 12.4 percent of the amount of the self-employment income for such taxable year".

Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 6 (line 4c plus line 5b; church employee income stops the return when /hadChurchEmployeeIncome is yes), and $0 when line 4c is under $400 ("stop; you don’t owe self-employment tax"). Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 11
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 11: "Multiply line 6 by 2.9% (0.029)". 26 U.S.C. 1401(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401#b_1): "2.9 percent of the amount of the self-employment income". Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 12: "Self-employment tax. Add lines 10 and 11."

Fact.Name: Secondary filer: Schedule SE line 13
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 13: "Deduction for one-half of self-employment tax. Multiply line 12 by 50% (0.50)", rounded to whole dollars as printed on that filer's Schedule SE. 26 U.S.C. 164(f)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164#f): "an amount equal to one-half of the taxes imposed by section 1401 (other than the taxes imposed by section 1401(b)(2))".

Fact.Name: Self-employment income: Schedule SE line 6, combined for both spouses
Fact.Description: Sum of each filer's Schedule SE line 6 (/primaryFilerSeIncome + /secondaryFilerSeIncome). Form 8959 line 13 reads it: 2026 draft Instructions for Form 8959 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i8959--dft.pdf, SHA-256 c5b1661eeb6cb33be840a0a01616d477d2731d2b3928e1bcd3fa13b1494bbaf1), PDF p. 5, Line 13: "Enter your self-employment income from Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part I, line 6. Combine amounts from this line if you have multiple Schedules SE." A spouse's loss is floored on that spouse's own Schedule SE, so it doesn't reduce the other spouse's self-employment income.

Fact.Name: SE tax applies to either filer
Fact.Description: True when either filer's Schedule SE line 4c is $400 or more (26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(2)).

Fact.Name: Self-employment tax (Schedule 2 line 4)
Fact.Description: Combined SE tax: each filer's Schedule SE line 12 added together. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE. Include the total profits or losses from all businesses on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Enter the combined SE tax on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4."

Fact.Name: Deductible part of self-employment tax (Schedule 1 line 15)
Fact.Description: Each filer's Schedule SE line 13 added together. 26 U.S.C. 164(f)(1) gives each individual a deduction of one-half of their own 1401 taxes. 2026 draft Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 15: "Deductible part of self-employment tax. Attach Schedule SE". Flows to /adjustmentsToIncome (taxCalculations.xml) and to Schedule 8812 line 22 through /schedule1Line15.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE out-of-scope questions apply
Fact.Description: Farm profit (Schedule F, lines 1a and 1b), church employee income, an optional method, ministry or a Form 4361 or Form 4029 exemption, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages are asked when the filer has Schedule C self-employment income or a nonzero Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a). A K-1-only return still has net earnings from that box. Complete false when neither applies, including when /hadSelfEmploymentIncome is unanswered and box 14 code A is not nonzero.

Fact.Name: Farm self-employment income
Fact.Description: Yes when Schedule F farm profit or Conservation Reserve Program payments belong on Schedule SE lines 1a or 1b, or when the filer wants the farm optional method (Part II line 15). 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) and 1402(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a_1): net earnings include farm income, and certain CRP payments to a person receiving Social Security or disability benefits are excluded. The farm optional method is the flush language of 1402(a) and the limits in 1402(l). This tool does not compute lines 1a, 1b, or 15.

Fact.Name: Church employee income
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has church employee income for Schedule SE lines 5a and 5b. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(14) and 1402(j) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#j): that income is not reduced by deductions, is not combined with other net earnings, and uses a $100 floor instead of $400.

Fact.Name: Elects the nonfarm optional method
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer elects the nonfarm optional method (Schedule SE line 4b and Part II lines 16 and 17). 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a), the nonfarm optional-method sentences at the end of subsection (a), and 1402(l). The farm optional method is /hadFarmSelfEmploymentIncome and still stops the return. The election is used only when /primaryFilerNonfarmOptionalMethodApplies or /secondaryFilerNonfarmOptionalMethodApplies is true.

Fact.Name: Net earnings of at least $400 in two of the prior three years
Fact.Description: Yes when actual net earnings from self-employment were $400 or more in 2 of the 3 consecutive tax years immediately preceding the year the nonfarm optional method is used. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, and 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a). Asked only after /usesSeOptionalMethod is yes.

Fact.Name: Nonfarm optional method used fewer than five prior years
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has used the nonfarm optional method in fewer than five earlier years, so this year is not the sixth or later use. The five years do not have to be consecutive. 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3: "You may use this method no more than five times." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7. A no stops the return. Asked only after /usesSeOptionalMethod is yes.

Fact.Name: Minister, religious order, or SE tax exemption
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer is a minister, a member of a religious order, or a Christian Science practitioner, or has an approved Form 4361 or Form 4029 exemption. 26 U.S.C. 1402(c)(4) treats that service as a trade or business. 1402(a)(8) computes net earnings without the section 107 housing exclusion. 1402(e) is the Form 4361 exemption and 1402(g) is the Form 4029 exemption (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#e). Checkbox A and the housing amount are not computed here.

Fact.Name: Notary fees excluded from self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has notary fees excluded from net earnings. 26 U.S.C. 1402(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#c_1): the performance of the functions of a public office is not a trade or business. The Schedule SE instructions subtract those fees from line 3 or require "Exempt—Notary." This tool does not make that subtraction.

Fact.Name: Form 8919 wages
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has wages from Form 8919 that belong on Schedule SE line 8c. Those wages are social-security wages for the wage-base limit. income /wagesFrom8919 is $0, so a yes stops the return instead of leaving line 8c blank. Asked when /scheduleSEOutOfScopeQuestionsApply is true. Form 4137 tips already stop the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips) and are Schedule SE line 8b.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule SE line this tool does not compute
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when /scheduleSEOutOfScopeQuestionsApply is true and the filer answers yes to farm profit, Conservation Reserve Program payments, or the farm optional method (Schedule SE lines 1a, 1b, and Part II line 15; 26 U.S.C. 1402(a), 1402(a)(1), and 1402(l)), church employee income (lines 5a and 5b; 1402(a)(14) and 1402(j)), ministry or a Form 4361 or Form 4029 exemption (1402(a)(8), 1402(c)(4), 1402(e), 1402(g)), notary fees excluded as a public office (1402(c)(1)), or Form 8919 wages (line 8c). The nonfarm optional method is /flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethod, not this fact. The gate is Schedule C self-employment income or a nonzero Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A. Complete and false when that gate is not true, including when /hadSelfEmploymentIncome is unanswered and box 14 code A is not nonzero, and when every question is answered no. An unanswered question while the gate is true stays incomplete, so those lines are not filed as zero.

Fact.Name: Knockout: nonfarm optional method is not allowed on this return
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when the filer elects the nonfarm optional method and the election cannot be used. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) and 1402(l). 2026 draft Schedule SE, PDF p. 3, and 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 7. The election stops when Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A is nonzero (code C is not collected), when a filer with Schedule C activity fails the dollar tests or line 17 would be less than actual net earnings, when neither filer has Schedule C activity, when net earnings were not at least $400 in 2 of the prior 3 years, or when this would be the sixth or later use. A claim of the earned income credit, the additional child tax credit, or the child and dependent care credit is /flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethodCredits and is not part of this fact, so this section can be complete before those credits are answered. Complete false when the election is unanswered or no, so the regular method still files. An unanswered election while the Schedule SE questions apply stays incomplete.

Fact.Name: Knockout: nonfarm optional method together with the EITC, ACTC, or CDCC
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when the nonfarm optional method applies and the return claims the earned income credit, the additional child tax credit, or the child and dependent care credit. Line 4b is not added to earned income. 26 U.S.C. 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) measures net earnings with the section 164(f) deduction. Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, uses Schedule SE line 3 minus line 13, not line 4b. 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5, lines 4 and 5: "If you use either optional method to figure net earnings, subtract any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15, from the total of the amounts shown on Schedule SE (Form 1040), lines 3 and 4b." /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome stays Schedule C line 31 minus the deductible part of self-employment tax, so an election that applies cannot be filed with /isReceivingEitc, /isReceivingActc, or /cdccQualified. Not part of /scheduleCSectionIsComplete: those credits are asked later, and an unanswered credit must not leave the Schedule C section incomplete. Complete false when neither filer's method applies, including when the election is unanswered or no, without reading the credits.

Fact.Name: Schedule C section complete
Fact.Description: Interview complete when there is no Schedule C and no nonzero Form 1065 box 14 code A, or when Schedule C is finished, the Schedule SE out-of-scope questions are answered no, and the nonfarm optional method is not stopped for eligibility. The credit conflict (/flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethodCredits) is not part of this fact. A K-1-only return still has to answer those questions. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a).
